name: Photomontage
summary: Fragments of photographs, cut and joined on one sheet, so that the joins make a statement that no single photograph makes.
how: Join 3 to 12 photographic fragments on one ground and keep the cut edges hard and visible.
Vary the scale of the fragments by 4:1 or more, so that the joins read as a claim and not as a scene.
Set type as one more fragment, turned 0° to 30°, in the same stack of layers.

origin.note: Raoul Hausmann and Hannah Höch of Berlin Dada cut press photographs and paste them into one sheet.

adoptions.via: Alexander Rodchenko and El Lissitzky use photomontage in Constructivist posters and books.
Sergei Eisenstein carries the collision of fragments into the cut of Strike and Battleship Potemkin.
Punk zines and record sleeves cut up newspapers with scissors and glue.
Photoshop makes the cut and the layer digital; early cyberculture prints dense photo-illustration.
Designers cut photographs of objects and clouds into collage scenes, in the line of the Surrealist collages of Max Ernst.
